objectives.objective: Approach a floor mark with the cassette lowered
objectives.basis: The reset cases bring the empty cassette from the launch angle to the floor pickup pose on the commanded slide law.

objectives.objective: Seat the floor NOTE between the powered belts
objectives.basis: The acquire cases follow the recorded free NOTE over the lip to its seat and through the seat-confirmation dwell.

objectives.objective: Carry the NOTE while raising the mechanism
objectives.basis: The lift cases follow the recorded NOTE on the commanded 4.8 s lift. Driving and turning during the lift are covered by the route screens, not by this check.

objectives.objective: Feed and deliver the NOTE through the speaker opening
objectives.basis: The feed and flight cases follow the recorded NOTE from the feed command through full passage of the opening. Counter registration is recorded in the pinned shot trial.

objectives.objective: Six scores in 120 s on at least 19 of 20 frozen starts
objectives.basis: Not shown. A layout check cannot show a statistical target, and the simulation does not support it: every perturbed NOTE is delivered through the opening from the firing lane, but about nine in ten are counted by the speaker within 7 s. It is carried in the risk register as a bench test with pass and fail counts.
The stow case returns the empty cassette to the parked angle. The PARK route on the field is covered by the endgame route study.

The approach, capture, hoist and hold cases follow the recorded forward centre-of-gravity climb from the parked cassette to the disabled hold on the slide stops. The working chain and the stage are not in the layout solids; chain contact is in the pinned climb trial.
Depends on a partner robot. No shared-chain geometry is designed.
The narrative leaves the entry pose undefined. No source pickup is designed.

presentation.title: Guided cassette 1.1 · preliminary design
presentation.architecture: Floor pickup over a removable lip into a pivoting cassette on a translating truck, a close-range speaker shot from split feed and launch belts, and a two-hook guided climb on the same pivot drive
presentation.focus: Play the cycle in order: reset, acquire, lift, feed, flight, stow, then approach, capture, hoist and hold. The NOTE follows the recorded free-body trial and the climb follows its recorded trial; the cassette and truck follow their commanded laws. Then open the weight and voltage ledgers: 0.43 kg and 0.34 V are the smallest margins.
notes: Firing lane: robot centre 1.39 m from the alliance wall at y = 5.821 m, cassette at 122 degrees. The cycle trials fired from y = 5.871 m; the single-shot campaign moved the lane 50 mm toward the centre of the opening, where the side clearance is larger.

From the firing lane 34 of 34 perturbed NOTES pass through the opening and 31 are counted by the speaker within 7 s. The uncounted NOTES, watched for 20 s, came back out through the opening without reaching either beam, so delivered and eventually counted is not met for them. Six scores in 120 s on 19 of 20 starts is not shown. Both are carried as bench tests.

The 232 solids are the draft layout with repaired component names and one revision: both launch belt motors are raised 60 mm along the cassette normal on lengthened drive shafts, because the whole-cycle check found no clearance between their cans and the floor NOTE riding over the pickup lip. The pickup trial does not model the motors.

NOTE paths and the cover leaf angle are recorded simulation output. Cassette angle, truck position and chassis motion are commanded laws. Each case states how far its straight path departs from the trace.
Declared NOTE indentation limits are planning assumptions. No measured force or allowable is claimed.
The upper inspection estimate of 56.270 kg includes a 3 to 6 kg unallocated design reserve.
The layout STEP draws the cover leaf closed at the parked angle. The cam law of the trials holds it open above 102 degrees, and the cycle cases follow the cam law.

uncoveredCases.reason: Six scores in 120 s on 19 of 20 starts is not supported by simulation. From the firing station every one of 34 perturbed carried NOTES passes through the opening, but 31 (91%) shadow both speaker beams within 7 s; six in a row at that rate is about 57%. Across all 1742 perturbed shots of the campaign 1398 were delivered and 1290 counted. The count rate did not move with launcher speed (6.56 to 7.68 m/s) or with the speaker's counter drive speed; the friction of the speaker surfaces was not varied. The 3 uncounted NOTES at the firing station bounce out. Watched for 20 s, each enters 0.54 to 0.63 m past the opening, returns through the opening within 3 s without shadowing either beam and comes to rest on the carpet in front of the speaker. None counts late and none stays in the speaker (4 NOTES watched in all, one of them at 123 degrees: 0 counted late, 0 stayed, 4 bounced out). The owner's criterion, wholly through the opening and eventually counted, is NOT met for those 3 NOTES. That is an open finding for the owner. Nothing recorded at release separates them: launch speed, elevation, lateral velocity, peak height and opening margin all lie inside the range of the counted NOTES. They are the carries R02-inner, R03-center-mid and R03-outer, which bounce out in 15 to 18 percent of their deliveries across the campaign while five other carries never do, so the cause travels with the incoming NOTE state. NOTE attitude and spin at the opening were not compared. A NOTE that bounces out touches none of the counter parts that every counted NOTE touches. The frozen full-mission campaign at the trial station failed three of its first seven starts. What happens to a NOTE inside the speaker rests on assumed field conveyor speeds and friction, so the deciding evidence is a real speaker.

uncoveredCases.condition: Real speaker counting a delivered NOTE
uncoveredCases.reason: In simulation 31 of 34 perturbed NOTES delivered from the firing station are counted within 7 s (median 4.1 s, latest 5.2 s after the shot starts). The other 3 are not late: they bounce back out through the opening within 3 s and are never counted. Six scores on 19 of 20 starts needs more than 99 in 100. The delay and the bounce-outs are properties of the modelled speaker interior and are unmeasured.

uncoveredCases.condition: Chassis position and heading error at the firing station
uncoveredCases.reason: The cycle trials fired from y = 5.871 m, where the NOTE cleared the side of the opening by 17.6 mm and a 2 degree heading error or a 50 mm lateral error lost every shot. The release moves the firing lane to y = 5.821 m (56.7 mm smallest margin). There every shot is delivered over heading errors of -3 to 4 deg, lateral positions of 5.796 to 5.871 m and stations of 1.39 to 1.45 m from the alliance wall, one input changed at a time. Errors combine: at 122 degrees, 20 mm toward the side wall with 3 degrees of heading error let 1 of 34 NOTES count, while 2 degrees with the same 20 mm delivered and counted all 12 nominal NOTES. The bench values are therefore the combined window, not the single-input one. The rear bumper is 35 mm from the subwoofer at the firing station, and stations nearer the wall were not fired. Chassis tracking to that window is unmeasured.

uncoveredCases.condition: Chassis lateral error at the firing station
uncoveredCases.reason: With 2 degrees of heading error present, delivery and counting held at 20 mm of lateral error either way on the nominal NOTES. From the trial lane, 50 mm toward the side wall lost every NOTE. Lateral tracking is unmeasured.

uncoveredCases.condition: Chassis fore-aft error at the firing station
uncoveredCases.reason: At 122 degrees delivery holds 30 mm farther from the alliance wall with 32.2 mm of opening margin and 60 mm farther with 7.6 mm; at 100 mm farther 16 of 34 NOTES miss the opening.

uncoveredCases.condition: Launch belts below their commanded speed at feed
uncoveredCases.reason: At the trial lane every perturbed NOTE is delivered for launcher commands of 6.56 to 7.68 m/s. On the nominal NOTES delivery holds down to 6.08 m/s, loses 1 of 6 at 5.92 m/s and loses every NOTE at 5.60 m/s and below. Belt speed at feed on a weak pack is unmeasured; the voltage test does not measure it.

uncoveredCases.condition: NOTE ejected from the speaker back onto the robot
uncoveredCases.reason: In start R02 the third NOTE left the speaker and entered the roboRIO envelope by up to 25.0 mm. No guard is drawn. Detailed design fits a guard over the electrical bay, charged to the unallocated reserve.

uncoveredCases.condition: Floor NOTE more than 50 mm off the cassette centre
uncoveredCases.reason: The pickup seats a NOTE 50 mm off centre on either side and first fails at 100 mm on either side; no offset between was tried. Driver or vision alignment to that band is unmeasured.

uncoveredCases.condition: Centre of gravity more than 50 mm ahead of nominal
uncoveredCases.reason: After power cut the climb holds 11.5 mm above the carpet with the centre of gravity 40 mm ahead of nominal, 10.9 mm at 50 mm and 8.4 mm at 60 mm, against a 10 mm allowance. Rearward it passes to 120 mm. The centre of gravity is unmeasured.

uncoveredCases.condition: Battery lifted out at the service index
uncoveredCases.reason: The straight 370 mm battery lift at the service index is not a checked case: the disconnected pack lead is not represented and the lift does not yet pass. The checked service case is the index pin withdrawal. An earlier service-lock study reported 5 mm smallest clearance for this lift; it has not been repeated on the revised layout.

uncoveredCases.condition: Reach and height through chain capture and hoist
uncoveredCases.reason: No file of this release states the largest reach beyond the frame or the largest height through chain capture and hoist. At floor pickup the furthest forward point is 640.0 mm sampled (642.3 mm bounded) against the project front limit of 644.8 mm, which is 304.8 mm beyond the frame.
